eligibility_reason: The authors genotyped a new, independent sample of 2474 Milwaukee African Americans to test SNP associations with hypertension/blood pressure previously reported by the Adeyemo et al. (2009) GWAS and by the STK39 (Wang et al. 2009) and CDH13 (Org et al. 2009) GWAS; the title calls it a 'Non-replication study'.

effects.original_title: A genome-wide association study of hypertension and blood pressure in African Americans
effects.original_authors: Adeyemo, A; Gerry, N; Chen, G; Herbert, A; Doumatey, A; Huang, H; Zhou, J; Lashley, K; Chen, Y; Christman, M; Rotimi, C
effects.replication_study: single study (Milwaukee African American case-control sample, n = 2474)
effects.outcome: Association of the GWAS-identified SNPs (genome-wide significant for SBP in/near PMS1, SLC24A4, YWHAZ, IPO7, CACNA1H, plus the other top-associated SNPs for hypertension status, SBP and DBP; 16 SNPs in all) with hypertension status and systolic/diastolic blood pressure
effects.contrast: minor vs major allele / genotype of each SNP (hypertensive cases vs normotensive controls; BP as a quantitative trait)
effects.description: In the first GWAS of African Americans, several SNPs in or near PMS1, SLC24A4, YWHAZ, IPO7 and CACNA1H reached genome-wide significance for systolic blood pressure (with further top-associated SNPs for hypertension status and diastolic BP).
effects.citation_sentence: In the first ever GWAS in African Americans (all subjects were residents of the Washington DC area), Adeyemo et al identified several SNPs reaching genome-wide significance for systolic blood pressure in or near genes: PMS1, SLC24A4, YWHA7, IPO7, and CACANA1H [18]. ... Therefore, we investigated the association of SNPs identified by Adeyemo et al in an independent population of African American subjects from the mid-western United States.
effects.evidence: Discussion, para 1: "In this sample of African Americans, none of the SNPs evaluated were convincingly associated with hypertension as a binary trait or with blood pressure level as a quantitative trait. Thus, we were unable to confirm previously reported associations between PMS1, SLC24A4, YWHA7, IPO7, and CACANA1H with systolic and diastolic blood pressure." Conclusions: "Results of the current study and others do not replicate previously identified hypertension-related SNPs in GWAS." Tables 2-3: all additive-model and regression p-values non-significant.
effects.notes: Enumeration choice: Adeyemo's SNP findings are coded as one entry. Its headline claim is the genome-wide-significant SBP loci (Methods: 'Among these SNPs, only a few had reached genome-wide significance for systolic BP'); the HTN-binary and DBP top SNPs were sub-genome-wide-significant top hits, not separate claimed findings. A second coder could split the entry into three (HTN status, SBP, DBP), as candidate luna56 did; all three would be failure. Nominal hits (rs12748299 with SBP in normotensives, p=0.002, lost after covariate adjustment and with lower rather than higher SBP; rs2146204 recessive p=0.006, SBP p=0.02) were not significant after correction, and the authors frame the study as a non-replication. Replication type: same ancestry, new independent sample. The methods differ (targeted TaqMan genotyping, case-control design with low-BP controls, no principal-component adjustment) and the authors do not label the replication type. Coded direct per the direct-vs-close tiebreaker; close experiment or close extension is also defensible (different US region; the authors note admixture and allele-frequency differences). Original DOI from the paper's XML reference list (ref 18).

effects.original_title: Whole-genome association study identifies STK39 as a hypertension susceptibility gene
effects.original_authors: Wang, Y; O'Connell; McArdle; Wade; Dorff; Shah; Shi; Pan; Rampersaud; Shen
effects.original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
effects.replication_study: single study (Milwaukee African American case-control sample, n = 2474)
effects.outcome: Association of common STK39 variants (4 SNPs tested: rs2063958, rs2390639, rs11890527, rs2203703) with systolic/diastolic blood pressure and hypertension status
effects.contrast: minor vs major allele / genotype of each STK39 SNP
effects.description: A GWAS in Amish subjects found strong association of common variants in the serine/threonine kinase gene STK39 with systolic and diastolic blood pressure, identifying STK39 as a hypertension susceptibility gene.
effects.citation_sentence: To minimize environmental and genetic variability, Wang et al carried out a GWAS of systolic and diastolic blood pressure in Amish subjects [11]. Strong association signals with several common variants in a serine/threonine kinase gene (STK39) were found and they confirmed these associations in an independent Amish and 4 non-Amish Caucasian samples [11].
effects.evidence: Discussion (STK39 paragraph): "We were unable to confirm the associations of 2 top-associated SNPs in this gene for systolic and diastolic blood pressure in our cohort despite having adequate power." Tables 2-3: all STK39 SNP p-values >= 0.10.
effects.notes: Methods: '8 variants in 2 genes (STK39 and CHD13) identified in European and Amish populations [11,14] and replicated by Adeyemo et al [18] in African Americans were also selected for replication in the current study.' The SNPs tested appear to be the ones Adeyemo et al. reported in this gene, so the claim under test is the gene-level STK39-BP association; Wang et al. is the originating finding. SBP and DBP are endpoints of this one claim, so they form one entry. Coded close extension because the population differs in ancestry (African Americans vs Amish/Caucasians). The extracted reference list garbles the author names after Wang (e.g. 'Connell O', 'Mcardle J'), so only surnames are given and initials are left out instead of guessed. Verify them against the PDF reference list. DOI from the paper's XML reference list (ref 11).

effects.original_title: Genome-wide scan identifies CDH13 as a novel susceptibility locus contributing to blood pressure determination in two European populations
effects.original_authors: Org, E; Eyheramendy, S; Juhanson, P; Gieger, C; Lichtner, P; Klopp, N; Veldre, G; Doring, A; Viigimaa, M; Sober, S
effects.replication_study: single study (Milwaukee African American case-control sample, n = 2474)
effects.outcome: Association of CDH13 variants (4 SNPs tested: rs11860907, rs7200009, rs16960421, rs17177428) with hypertension status and systolic/diastolic blood pressure
effects.contrast: minor vs major allele / genotype of each CDH13 SNP
effects.description: A GWAS in a German population identified the CDH13 (Cadherin 13) locus as a novel susceptibility locus contributing to blood pressure determination.
effects.citation_sentence: Another novel locus contributing to blood pressure was identified by Org et al in a GWAS of a German population and is known as Cadherin 13-Heart (CDH13) [14].
effects.evidence: Discussion (CDH13 paragraph): "We tested the association of 4 of these SNPs with hypertension as a binary trait and blood pressure as a quantitative trait in our sample. We confirmed a borderline association (insignificant when considered with multiple tests) of rs17177428 and rs7200009 with blood pressure as quantitative trait among hypertensive and normotensive subjects." Results: rs7200009 SBP/DBP p = 0.04 and rs17177428 SBP p = 0.04 in hypertensives (unadjusted), not significant after correction; Tables 2-3 null.
effects.notes: The authors' own wording is hedged: they 'confirmed a borderline association', but one that is 'insignificant when considered with multiple tests'. The association appears only in subgroup analyses (hypertensives or normotensives separately) and only at nominal significance. The case-control and regression analyses are null, and the paper's title and conclusion frame everything as a non-replication. Coded inconclusive per the failure-vs-inconclusive tiebreaker and the 'limited support' wording; failure is a strong competing reading. The SNPs tested were those Adeyemo et al. reported in this locus. SBP and DBP are endpoints of one claim, so they form one entry. Coded close extension because the population differs in ancestry (African Americans vs Germans/Europeans). DOI from the paper's XML reference list (ref 14).
